youtube.title: Goblin Tools: one chore became 33 steps (94/100)
youtube.description:
Not sponsored. No affiliate link, and Goblin Tools didn't pay for this.

Goblin Tools is a free website that breaks a chore into small steps. We typed one chore, "clean the garage", into its Magic ToDo and tried three spice levels (how far it breaks things down), one try each, no account.

Level 1: 6 steps in about a second. Level 3: 11 useful steps (sort into keep, donate or trash, sweep, set up shelves). Level 5: 33 steps, and it drifts from cleaning into repairs: patch the walls, repaint, oil the garage door.

Our score: 94/100 (quality 44/50, speed 15/15, free plan 25/25, price 10/10). Our best score so far.
Good for: chores you keep putting off. Not for: level 5 if you want a short list.
Tip: start at level 2 or 3. Level 5 adds jobs you never asked for.

Free: everything on the website, no account, no limit published. Paid: $3 a month (Goblin Tools Pro saves and syncs your lists and lets you share them).
All our scores: specimindlab.github.io/004 (link in our channel profile)

youtube.title: OpenAI's Sora lasted 7 months. What to use now
youtube.description:
Not sponsored. No affiliate links. Research only: Sora is shut down, so there was nothing left to test, and we give it no score.

OpenAI's Sora app launched on 30 Sep 2025 and closed on 26 Apr 2026, just under 7 months later. The last way in, OpenAI's developer access, closed on 24 Sep 2026. OpenAI says it deletes Sora data after the shutdown, so videos people didn't export are gone.

Three places to make AI videos now:
1. Wan (Alibaba): open source and free to download. Its free demo page wasn't working when we checked on 10 Oct.
2. Kling (Kuaishou): an app like Sora was, with free credits once you make an account (Kling doesn't publish how many).
3. Gemini Omni (Google): replaced Veo 3.1 in the Gemini app; paid plans only.

Lesson: keep your own copies of anything you make on an AI app. When it shuts down, your files can go with it.

All 3 links and the sources: specimindlab.github.io/X01 (link in our channel profile)

youtube.title: Liquid AI d1: it guessed 5 of our 6 drawings
youtube.description:
Not sponsored. No affiliate link, and Liquid AI didn't pay for this.

Liquid AI's d1 is a small, free AI that answers questions about pictures. Its free demo page has a game called Quick Draw: you draw a word, and it guesses while you draw, out of 16 possible words. We played one round (6 words), drawing our own simple line drawings stroke by stroke, no account.

It got 5 of 6: fish, clock, snowman, guitar and bicycle, in about 9 seconds each. It missed the apple, even though apple was its top guess the whole time: it stayed at 75%, and the game only accepts a guess at 85%.

Our score: 81/100 (quality 47/50, speed 15/15, free plan 16/25, price 3/10: no price published).
Good for: seeing how fast small AI has got. Not for: an everyday app. It's a demo.

Free: the demo page, no account; the model is free to download. Paid: not published.
Play it and see every score: specimindlab.github.io/005 (link in our channel profile)

youtube.title: Hookest: we asked AI for 5 hooks, 2 were usable
youtube.description:
Not sponsored. No affiliate link, and Hookest didn't pay for this.

Hookest is a free website that writes the first line of a short video (the "hook"). No signup. We described our own Goblin Tools video and asked for 5 hooks, one try, default settings.

It answered in 4.2 seconds. We rated each hook by our own rules: a real number or result from the test, true, no hype. 2 of 5 passed: "What if cleaning your garage had 33 steps instead of one?" and "This AI turned one task into dozens". One was clickbait ("You won't believe..."), two were too vague. And its best hook ran 4.2 seconds, past its own 3-second limit.

Our score: 77/100 (quality 27/50, speed 15/15, free plan 25/25, price 10/10).
Good for: a first draft of your hook. Not for: copying hooks without editing.
Tip: give it real numbers from your video, then cut the best hook to under 3 seconds.

Free: the hook generator, no signup. Paid: $9 a month (Hookest Pro).
The test and every score: specimindlab.github.io/006 (link in our channel profile)

youtube.title: Free Gemini changed Oct 9: what you lost
youtube.description:
Not sponsored. No affiliate links. Research only: we read Google's own help page, so there's no score.

From 9 October 2026, free Gemini accounts use "Auto": Gemini picks the model for each question. Most answers come from the smallest model (Flash-Lite); harder questions may still go to Flash or Pro. What you lost: choosing a model yourself. Turn Auto off and every answer comes from the small model.

Many headlines said free users "only get Flash-Lite". Google's own page is more careful than that.

Your three choices now:
1. Stay free: Auto, mostly the small model, Pro sometimes for hard questions.
2. Google AI Plus, $4.99 a month (US): the middle model, but it loses Pro too.
3. Google AI Pro, $19.99 a month (US): every model, plus Deep Think.

Limits now refresh every 5 hours up to a weekly cap, and Pro, images and video use them up faster.
Lesson: read the company's own page before the headlines.

Every plan and the sources: specimindlab.github.io/X02 (link in our channel profile)

youtube.title: LightOnOCR-3 read 42 of 46 handwritten words
youtube.description:
Not sponsored. No affiliate link, and LightOn didn't pay for this.

LightOnOCR-3 is a new free AI from LightOn that turns photos of pages into text. We gave its free demo one photo of a handwritten note (46 words, on the back of an old photo card), one try, no account, and checked it against our own word-by-word reading.

It read 42 of 46 words in about 4 seconds. But three mistakes change the story: "Mum" became "My own", the cat Butch became "Butel", and the last line, "Ginger Tom", became "thing. Love".

Our score: 54/100 (quality 20/50, speed 15/15, free plan 16/25, price 3/10: no price published). Skip it for handwriting you need word for word.
Good for: a quick first draft you'll check. Not for: when you need every word right.
Tip: always read OCR against the original, especially names and the last line.

Free: the demo page, no account; the model is free to download (Apache 2.0). Paid: not published.
The full test: specimindlab.github.io/007 (link in our channel profile)

Note photo: Annie Spratt on Unsplash.
